Team — kicking off the RSVP and tracking plan for the October Developer Live Sprint we’re co-hosting with Acme. Need a tight one-pager and small asset set to hand to ops and the partner by EOD tomorrow. Key asks: 

1) Copy for the developer invite (short, technical, 3 bullets showing value) — two subject line variants.
2) Target lists: engineer segments (backend, infra, ML infra) and a VIP list of customers + top prospects for personal outreach.
3) Tracking links & failover chain — canonical RSVP link, fallback link (if 302 fails), and a short UTM mapping for every touch.
4) VIP cadence: who owns 1:1 outreach and 24/48 hr reminder windows.

I’ve attached the initial_tracking_map_v1.xlsx with preliminary UTMs and the proposed link rotation. Please review and post edits/comments inline. CC’ing Jordan so the Acme team can confirm their tracking constraints (they sometimes require a single-domain redirect and prefer utm_source=acme).

Deliverable: final copy + final tracking_links_matrix by EOD Fri (10/9).

> Thanks Naomi — I’ll draft the two subject lines and the short invite copy...

Quick tech note on tracking/failover: attached is tracking_links_matrix_v2.xlsx with the full mapping. Summary: 

- Canonical RSVP: https://redwood.com/rsvp/dev-sprint?utm_source=redwood&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=dev_sprint_oct26
- Partner redirect (required by Acme): https://rsvp.acme.io/partner/redirect?id=rdw123 -> then forwards to canonical. If partner redirect returns 200 but blocks cookies, we use the fallback: https://links.redwood.com/r/dev-sprint (server-side redirect with token).
- UTMs: add utm_source={redwood|acme}, utm_content={segment}, utm_term={subjectVariant}. We recommend server-side parameter stitching for CTA clicks to keep source attribution when partner redirect strips params.

Action items for ops:
- Marissa: final subject/content variants (two)
- Ben: confirm VIP list and owner for 24/48 hour touchbacks
- Jordan: can Acme confirm they can maintain the utm_source=acme tag through the redirect chain? If not, we will rely on linkshortener fallback (links.redwood.com).

I’ve flagged a couple of entries in the sheet where the partner redirect will strip query params (rows 14–19).

—Mateo

Hi Naomi / team — confirmed on the redirect behavior. Acme’s redirect preserves the path but strips unknown query params in certain enterprise tenants. We can whitelist utm_source and utm_campaign if Redwood supplies the tag list (should be fine). I attached the note from our infra team outlining the policy. Our preference is utm_source=acme when the invite originates from our co-marketing send; otherwise utm_source=redwood.

We’ll accept the canonical redirect pattern and will add a whitelist rule for utm_source and utm_campaign. If you want to avoid extra work on our side, use the links.redwood.com fallback for opens/clicks — we’ll sync on analytics.  

Thanks — Jordan
